pr_title: Migrate Mock HTTP Proxy to Netty
pr_body:
Instead of using raw TCP sockets and parsing HTTP requests manually which is tends to be quite error-prone, we can create an HTTP proxy server using Netty. In contrast to `com.sun.net` a Netty HTTP server it can act as an HTTP proxy. Netty also supports a nonblocking HTTP client which we can leverage instead of using the blocking `HttpURLConnection`. 

This change also allows the server to be asynchronous and support persistent keep-alive connections. It should prevent creating excessive threads to handle new HTTP connection which matters when we run heavy tests in `GcsProxyIntegrationTests`.

Fixes #93824 
Fixes #93811 
Fixes #93816
pr_comments: @original-brownbear I've made a stab on re-using the event loop. It works, but we have to use boss and workers event loops in order to re-use them between different bootstraps. I'm not sure which version is better.

@arteam can you elaborate on why we can't share the loop for both the client and the server connections? That shouldn't be an issue, we do the same in the production tcp transport implementation as far as I can see?

@original-brownbear I've reverted the change. It turned out I was wrong: it does work a single threaded event loop. I must have some bug in the proxy implementation when I was moving to re-using the event loop, because it was totally not working. PTAL!
FWIW, I've also submitted #94205 as a blocking alternative to this PR
